messages.subject: Linked brush question
parts:
Hi,

after the "empty plot" issue caused by grouped data was fixed, I have modified the hflights test app to show two plots of fligth delays in different months - selectable by shiny selectinputs. 

Code is here:

https://github.com/ThomasSiegmund/ggvis-hflights/tree/master

Can be seen in action using

shiny::runGitHub("ggvis-hflights", "thomassiegmund")

Now I'd like to use the linked brush on these plots, to see e.g. where the heavily delayed connections from January show up in another month.

Documentation of linked_brush() says: 

keys: vector of all possible keys if known.

So I have constructed a linked brush using the FlightNum variable:

keys <- unique(DelayByFlightNum$FlightNum);
);
lb <- linked_brush(keys = keys, fill = "red")

This doesn't seem to work, maybe I misunderstood the doc. I always get:

Error : Length of calculated column 'reactive_68b7523e' (3740) is not equal to 1 or the number of rows in data (1).

Code of the example app with brush is at:

https://github.com/ThomasSiegmund/ggvis-hflights/tree/brush

Run it using 

shiny::runGitHub("ggvis-hflights", "thomassiegmund", ref="brush")

Any ideas? Can this work at all? There is no guarantee that all flight numbers show up in all months.

Thanks

Thomas

messages.author: b756a7daa2c2aa6d
messages.subject: Re: Linked brush question
parts:
Hi Thomas,

A key has to be unique for each row in the data.

Hadley

messages.author: dea7fe9fc1920d2f
messages.subject: Re: Linked brush question
parts:
> Can you provide a bit more detail about what you trying
to do with the brush?

In bioinformatics there is the so called MA plot. You measure the activity of a few thousand genes under two different conditions and plot baseline abundance vs. fold change (typically both on log scale) (http://puriney.github.io/visay/2013/07/04/ma-plot-and-volcano-plot). Each dot represents a single gene. In an interactive version I'd like to identify the gene behind a dot using a tool tip or right button menu. Searching for a single gene of interest might also be useful.

The brush comes into place when there are more than two conditions. Say you have e.g. tested a certain cell type under two conditions, and now try the same conditions on a different cell type. The genes would be the same, but with more or less different abuandance and fold change values. Which (groups of) genes behave the same, which show up in a completely different spot in a plot of the second experiment? So I'd put the second experiment in a second plot and link them via the brush.

In real live of course there are not only two experiments, so you would need to select the experiment on the fly from a larger data set. In todays ggvis I think I can work out almost everthing needed, but the problem of using a dynamic data set with the brush. In my test app
(https://github.com/ThomasSiegmund/ggvis-hflights/tree/brush) I've substituted the genes with flight numbers from hfligths. There is a reactive function which delivers the data to the plots as monthly subsets. But I have no idea how to use the brush with it. It seems to accept only a static data set. I've tried to make the number of rows in the data fixed and initialized the brush accordingly but this also did not work.

Thanks for your interest.

Thomas
